corrections.discipline: Append-only. The original report and this JSON are not rewritten; every amendment below is registered here and summarised in section 8 of ROUND69_REPORT.md.

items.was: An earlier draft reported minibatches_total = 501, derived as 128184 // 256 + 1.
items.now: 676, matching the 676 recorded gate-record entries and the 676 reconstructed plan minibatches. The 501 figure assumed every minibatch is full-256 and ignored the partial final chunk of each epoch; it is retained only as superseded_erroneous_minibatches_total correction evidence.
items.effect_on_results: None on any scientific quantity; the count was wrong, not the data.

items.was: Implied the exact minibatch membership was fully reproduced.
items.now: Downgraded to an aggregate cross-check: the shuffle is source-derivable and n_rows / early_free / late_free match per minibatch with zero mismatches, but per-entry member indices were not persisted on disk and remain unprovable.
items.effect_on_results: No number changes; the claim strength is reduced.

items.was: Stated that counterfactual action value would need a model forward pass or a PPO replay, both forbidden this round.
items.now: Withdrawn. A forward pass or a PPO replay could not settle the causal question either: on-policy chosen-action advantages are not causal action values under any permitted recomputation. The question is not identifiable from the saved on-policy data, and no computation allowed in this round would change that.
items.effect_on_results: The item moves from 'needs a forbidden computation' to 'not identifiable from saved data'.

items.was: Read as evidence that the late signal cannot separate SEND from SKIP.
items.now: Withdrawn as an inference. Both action groups showing positive chosen-action advantage says nothing about whether the expected policy gradient can separate the two actions; chosen-action advantage is measured against a critic baseline, not between actions. The SEND/SKIP breakdown is retained strictly as a descriptive distribution.
items.effect_on_results: Descriptive counts unchanged; no separability claim.

items.was: The L1 gap between late_head (mean 0.269) and the critic heads (78.07 / 3.73) invited a clip-suppression reading.
items.now: Withdrawn. The heads have different parameter counts, so their L1 gradient magnitudes are not comparable, and no clipping inference is drawn from the gap. The provable facts are only: late-actor signal is sparse (1.60% of rows), its residuals are positive-skewed, and the recorded late_head gradients are non-zero on all 96 batches. These are explicitly NOT designated as the root cause of anything.
items.effect_on_results: No number changes; an unsupported inference removed.

items.was: A delegation reminder flagged that update/gate_diag early_free and late_free are epoch-accumulated exposure counts and must not be divided by tape rows as if they were unique row shares.
items.now: Confirmed already satisfied by this audit and now stated explicitly: every row / target figure is rebuilt from the tapes as unique per batch, recorded exposures are cross-checked via unique * 4 epochs == recorded, mixed early+late rows are counted once, and the two buckets are disjoint. See exposure_vs_unique_counts.
items.effect_on_results: None; the audit already used the correct caliber.

exposure_vs_unique_counts.warning: update.early_free / update.late_free and the gate_diag equivalents are EPOCH-ACCUMULATED EXPOSURE counts across the 4 PPO epochs of a batch. They are NOT unique per-tape candidates and must not be divided by tape row totals as a row share.
exposure_vs_unique_counts.cross_check_rule: unique_per_batch * EPOCHS == recorded exposure, applied per batch for samples, early_free and late_free; all 96 batches agree (batch_cross_check_all_agree).
exposure_vs_unique_counts.mixed_row_accounting: rows_with_late_free and rows_early_only are disjoint partitions and sum exactly to free_rows, so a row carrying both an early and a late free candidate is counted once in the row denominator and never twice.

spot_check_first_batch.note: For s22 batch 0 the recorded 64/28 exposure corresponds to 16/7 unique free candidates (16*4=64, 7*4=28). The same recomputation for s33 batch 0 also yields 16/7 unique, not the 16/6 quoted in the delegation reminder; the on-disk value is 16/7 and the 16/6 figure does not reproduce. This affects no audit total, which uses the full 96-batch recomputation.

minibatch_reconstruction.superseded_value_bug: An earlier draft of this audit reported minibatches_total = 501, computed as all_rows_denominator_instances // MINIBATCH_STEPS + 1 (128184 // 256 + 1). That formula implicitly assumes every minibatch is a full 256 rows, which is false: each epoch's final chunk is partial, so the true count is the sum over batches of EPOCHS * ceil(samples / MINIBATCH_STEPS). The value 501 is wrong and is kept here only as documented correction evidence; it is superseded by the recorded 676 gate-record entries and the 676 plan minibatches, which agree exactly per batch.
minibatch_reconstruction.plan_vs_execution_note: The theoretical all-4-epoch plan and the actual recorded execution coincide per batch: for every one of the 96 batches the reconstructed plan length, the recorded gate_records length, update.minibatches and update.optimizer_steps are all equal, and each plan minibatch's n_rows, early_free and late_free match its recorded gate_record. The plan is therefore not a hypothetical alternative schedule but a reproduction of what ran.
minibatch_reconstruction.aggregate_cross_check_caveat: This is an AGGREGATE cross-check. The data-order shuffle is derivable from the frozen source and the per-minibatch aggregate counts match with zero mismatches, but the per-entry member indices of each minibatch were never persisted to disk. Agreement on n_rows / early_free / late_free therefore does not independently prove which specific rows sat in which minibatch.

deliverable2_decomposition.note: combined = lambda*A_task - A_cost = (lambda*R_task - R_cost) - (lambda*V_task - V_cost) exactly, because A = R - V for each critic; a multi-candidate joint decision is ONE training row (row weight 1) and its targets are not independent samples

withdrawn_inferences.counterfactual_action_value: Withdrawn. The earlier wording implied that a model forward pass or a PPO replay would answer whether late sending is worth it. It would not: on-policy chosen-action advantage is not a causal action value, and no recomputation permitted in a read-only round can make it one. The SEND/SKIP causal question is simply not identifiable from the saved on-policy data.
withdrawn_inferences.direction_separates_send_skip: Withdrawn. Both action groups carrying positive chosen-action advantage does not show that the expected policy gradient cannot separate SEND from SKIP. The chosen-action advantage compares the taken joint action with a critic baseline, never the two actions with each other. Kept strictly descriptive.
withdrawn_inferences.clip_suppression_from_magnitude_gap: Withdrawn. The late_head L1 (mean 0.269) versus task_value_head (78.07) and cost_head (3.73) gap cannot support a clipping or suppression inference: the heads carry different parameter counts, so raw L1 magnitudes are not comparable across them.
withdrawn_inferences.what_remains_provable: Only these facts stand: the late-actor signal is sparse (1.60% of rows, about 3 rows per minibatch), its combined-advantage residuals are positive-skewed (92.2% positive), and the recorded late_head gradients are non-zero on all 96 batches. None of these is designated as the unique root cause of the R68 greedy zero-change, and none licenses deleting messages, changing a threshold, or naming a single loss as the cause.
